title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has released a policy document outlining its response to a 2020 report on AI and public standards, highlighting upcoming actions and changes. The document provides the government's vision for ensuring AI aligns with key societal values and standards in the UK.

title: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education
description: The Department for Education’s (DfE) position on the use of generative AI in the education sector.
summary: The Department for Education is considering the role of generative AI in education, including its potential benefits and risks. This policy aims to establish a framework for the responsible use of generative AI in educational settings.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual are setting out their approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications, which was requested by the Education and other Secretaries of State. This policy is a response to concerns and inquiries about the impact of AI on the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This document assesses the impact of copyright laws on the development and use of artificial intelligence systems that incorporate existing copyrighted works. It explores the potential implications of copyright restrictions on AI development, innovation, and intellectual property.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has officially responded to a report on artificial intelligence, outlining its plans for the technology's development and use within the country, in part based on recommendations from the House of Lords Select Committee. The government aims to implement various measures to responsibly harness AI's benefits while mitigating its potential risks and negative consequences.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the terms of reference for a committee reviewing the impact of artificial intelligence on public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to guide the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: The Centre for Science and Policy (CSPL) submitted evidence to the Science and Technology Committee inquiry on governing artificial intelligence. The submission aimed to provide input on how to effectively manage the growing use of AI.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This document will explore the effects of artificial intelligence on regulations for medical products. It aims to implement the guidelines stated in the Artificial Intelligence White Paper regarding this issue.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the Defence organisation the world's most effective, efficient, and trusted AI user relative to its size. It aims to achieve this vision through the use of artificial intelligence in Defence operations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: This document outlines a plan for the Department for Transport (DfT) to work with the transport sector to use artificial intelligence in a safe and beneficial way. The plan aims to maximize the advantages of AI while minimizing its potential risks.
